unit.why: A first-person memorate. The author pressed the tzaddik R. David Moshe to word a letter the author's way, and only years later recognized that the tzaddik's own wording would have been better for him.
unit.boundary_note: Final words 'ממדריגותיו הנוראים.' are a heading for the next section (ד), not part of this story.

stories.start_quote: אלה אזכרה ואשפכה עלי נפשי כי בחורף
stories.end_quote: בעצת קדשו הי' נכלל כל העתיד בענין שלי
stories.summary_en: In winter 1887 the author pressured R. David Moshe all day until he wrote an important letter in the author's preferred wording. The tzaddik said in Yiddish that he gave in only out of love, though he believed the other wording was for the author's good. Nineteen years later the author saw that following the tzaddik's counsel would have spared him all his troubles.

tags.why: The tzaddik's counsel foresaw the author's whole future.
